title: International Trade and Balance of Payments
text: The balance of payments is a statistical statement that summarizes the economic transactions of a country with the rest of the world over a given period. It consists of the current account (trade in goods and services, income, and transfers), the capital account, and the financial account. A current account surplus means a country exports more than it imports; a deficit means the opposite. The United States has run persistent current account deficits since the 1980s, while countries like China and Germany have maintained surpluses. Exchange rates play a crucial role in international trade by affecting the relative prices of exports and imports. International institutions like the IMF and World Bank monitor global trade imbalances.
